title: Qiskit/OpenQASM assurance bridge latency hardening
changes_under_test: Cache immutable installed-toolchain version metadata instead of reparsing package metadata for every request.
Export the already canonical-lowered Qiskit circuit directly through qiskit.qasm3.dumps instead of running a redundant optimization-level-0 transpilation.
Copy the input QuantumCircuit only on a fail-closed return instead of on every verified request.
Measure import, normalization serialization, compiler optimization, semantic verification, Qiskit lowering, OpenQASM export, OpenQASM reparse, report serialization, and complete assurance separately.
forbidden_changes: No replacement of Qiskit's official OpenQASM parser or exporter

timing_protocol.warmup: One complete supported request before recorded cases.
timing_protocol.adapter_overhead_definition: (Qiskit import time + canonical Qiskit lowering and official OpenQASM export time) / compiler-only optimize_circuit time

verdicts.release_ready: Pass only when every safety, coverage, determinism, and latency gate passes.
verdicts.held: If the latency gate still fails, keep rqm-qiskit 0.3.0 unreleased and publish the exact unfavorable result.

limitations: Wall-clock timing is descriptive of the recorded local environment and is sensitive to host load.
The CI regression ceiling is intentionally broader than the frozen release gate and cannot establish release readiness.
This run contains no simulator, emulator, provider, or QPU execution evidence.
Qiskit level-3 measurements remain descriptive and do not establish superiority.
Operator equivalence up to global phase does not authorize controlled-subcircuit promotion.
